independent_reproduction.scope: test fixtures create TemporaryDirectory stores and tiny commands; no authoritative store or scientific job accessed

methodology_review: Measure.py instruments actual V2 pin/checked/history/directory functions while preserving and returning underlying results. Temporary stores contain 64 pending admissions and a separate sequence of eight real capacity-one tiny commands. Counts and timing are bounded direct observations, not extrapolated benchmarks.

Fixed source pin calls/bytes are correctly separated from history-dependent authenticated plan reads. Instrumentation, warm cache, fixture construction and lack of physical I/O counters limit performance interpretation; no cold-cache or throughput claim follows.
Query plan inspection is an empty fresh schema only. It supports the literal optimizer SCAN operations shown, not actual large-history query latency. The thousands-cycle objective remains unproven.
source_and_crash_review: Dispatcher source roster pins current dispatcher, incremental admission core and V2 queue/execution/ledger/receipt sources; module path identity checks guard mixed imports. Tests reproduced refusal of changed roster, mixed imports, and V2-domain reuse before lock/root mutation.

Nine tests reproduced: transaction crash before/after evidence and claims plus exact retry, competing admission ownership/one launch, source mismatch and import/domain rejection, consumer launch recheck, crash points around dependency publication, nonzero/unknown predecessor retention, and tamper checks. This supports bounded failure handling under the trusted local process/filesystem model.

Atomic SQLite transaction prevents a half-published admission claim in tested crashes. Existing filesystem scaffold publication and recovery follows exact-equality checks; no automatic scaffold repair or cancellation is provided.
remaining_gaps: Mutable SQLite/config/evidence trust boundary remains explicit: a party able to rewrite database and files can forge/change the asserted local state; digests are not signatures or external historical audit.
SQL still scans historical reservation and owner rows; query plans were measured at empty-store only. Recursive shared-ancestor work and repeated whole-plan validation can expand with DAGs.
Tests cover small synthetic chains and fault points, not large scale, crash/power-loss/filesystem guarantees, malicious concurrent same-UID actors, or thousands of cycles.
No V2 integration, unattended controller, scientific result, performance improvement, qualification or production adoption is demonstrated.
recommendation: Retain as isolated research evidence. Any integration requires separate review of SQL indexing/frontier design and trust contract, then scale and recovery tests at representative non-scientific sizes before adoption.
